body.statement: For \(\mathfrak E_\star\) with uniform \(q\), \(F_{\mathcal J}=107/72\) and \(F_{\mathcal J,2}=F_{\mathcal J,3}=55/36\), so the exact gap is \(1/24\). By the strict class-inclusion proposition, every quadratic candidate allowed by the published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje framework lies in the Boolean comparison class \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\); hence the same \(55/36\) lower certificate rules out every such published candidate, although it does not assert that \(55/36\) is the optimum of their smaller positive-semidefinite class. The displayed bounds satisfy \(r^\star(\theta)-b^\star(\theta)=[1+x_0x_1x_2x_5]/24\in\{0,1/12\}\), and \(b^\star(\theta)=3^{-1}\sum_{z=1}^3h_z^\star(\theta|_{O_z})\) with every table entry in \([0,5]\). The distribution \(\mu^\star\) certifies \(107/72\), and \(\nu^\star\) certifies \(55/36\), by exact observable-margin equalities and complementary slackness across all sixty-four schedules.
body.justification: This exact nonnegative certificate proves that the published quadratic comparison class is globally incomplete even for a small legal binary experiment.
body.gap: \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} optimizes only quadratic forms, and \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} sharpens one factorial variance without an arbitrary-design degree separation; neither contains this quartic witness or the \(1/24\) rational gap.
body.consumer: It gives a reproducible test instance for variance-bound software and a concrete design where a higher-order rule pointwise improves a best observable quadratic rule.
